definition: Terse means using very few words, sometimes to the point of abruptness.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word terse. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know terse should be able to work it out from your sentence.

The magazine's new copy chief communicates in margin notes, and the notes are terse.
'Cut.' 'Why?' 'Prove it.' Rarely more than two words, never a greeting, and — the staff agrees — always a faint draft of cold air coming off the page.
Nobody calls the notes rude.
They are correct, useful, and instantly clear.
But interns who grew up on encouraging teachers learn to steel themselves before opening a marked-up draft.
One veteran writer shrugs at the complaints: the chill, she says, is the price of an editor who wastes no ink and spares no feelings.
